preparation.title: Festival preparation photograph
preparation.body: A red paper crane and a white ribbon mark desk 17. The other decorations are blue. Desk numbers 12, 17 and 31 are visible.
preparation.reverse:
15 October 1999. Festival committee.
Aya Ito: classroom decorations.
Keep the desk lids clear until cleanup.

original.title: The small original photograph
original.body: Sakiko sits at a desk holding scissors. She has just looked up. Her expression is reserved. She is not smiling.
original.reverse:
Sakiko. Festival preparations, 15 October 1999.
The photograph has been folded once, face inward.

folded.title: Folded note from desk 17
folded.body: Take it down before she sees it.

sketch.title: Festival mounting sketch
sketch.body:
ASSEMBLY
Position 1: RED FAN
Position 2: WHITE LANTERN
Position 3: BLUE STAR

Place each loose decoration on its matching numbered mount. The shallow drawer opens when all three mounting catches are seated.
sketch.reverse:
Ken Sato
Art room display materials
15 October 1999

display.title: The enlarged festival portrait
display.body: An enormous cardboard head hangs above the attraction. The enlarged photograph has uneven dark eyes and a grotesque smile painted over the mouth. Strings support the cardboard. Black strips trail below it.
display.reverse:
Ken Sato / display frame.
Return the two entrance keys after dismantling.
The face in the print has the same fringe as the small photograph.

recording.title: Festival recording / captions
recording.body:
[Student chatter]
“Does it hang straight?”
“Put the spare equipment case on shelf B two.”
[Laughter]
[Three quiet knocks]
“Is that part of the attraction?”
“Leave it. We still have cleanup.”

Equipment shelf B2 is labeled beside the audiovisual cabinet.
recording.reverse:
Mika Endo / AV equipment
Festival tape, 15 October 1999

account.title: A handwritten account
account.body:
I gave the key to you after cleanup.
You said you were going back.
Please stop saying we all forgot.
account.reverse:
Mika Endo
The reverse is otherwise blank.

plan.title: Maintenance plan
plan.body:
OLD SCENERY STORE
Behind the archive shelving, south end of the old wing.

To move the archive shelf: lift its floor brake, then slide it left. Keep the doorway clear.

Festival scenery was moved here after the attraction closed.
plan.reverse:
Service copy / 1999
Room location: south archive, east wall recess.

letter.title: Sakiko’s undelivered letter
letter.body:
Could I help in the library next year instead?
I know the festival needs people.
I would rather do something where nobody has to look at me.
letter.reverse:
No address. No stamp.
The paper was folded inside a small school bag.

belongings.title: A discarded festival tag
belongings.body:
Yui Kanda
SCENERY / FINAL CLEANUP
Return entrance key with the costume bag.

class_photo.title: A class photograph
class_photo.body: A class photograph from autumn 1999. Sakiko stands near the left edge, a little apart, behind a classmate’s shoulder. Her expression is reserved.
class_photo.reverse:
Class 1-A / autumn 1999
Sakiko’s name is written at the left margin.

notice.title: School notice
notice.body:
18 October 1999

We regret to inform families of the death of student Sakiko following an accident in a restricted scenery storage room.

Festival activities are suspended. Please direct inquiries to the school office.
notice.reverse: Office copy. No names appear beneath the printed statement.

inventory.title: Festival inventory
inventory.body:
15 October 1999

3 mounting decorations
1 hanging frame
1 oversized portrait
1 scenery-room key

Return borrowed equipment to shelf B2.
inventory.reverse:
Ken Sato / Mika Endo
The portrait entry has been circled.

destroy.title: A later message
destroy.body:
Please destroy the old festival photographs.
I do not want another copy turning up.
Ask the others as well.

maintenance.title: Caretaker’s maintenance sheet
maintenance.body:
16 October 1999

08:40  Scenery storeroom opened.
Student found shortly afterward. Police notified.

18:10  Returned to secure storeroom.
Knocking heard [u]inside[/u].

The word “inside” is underlined twice in the handwritten original.
maintenance.reverse:
Caretaker’s duplicate.
Both entries are in the same handwriting.
